papers.title: Rebellious Student: Reversing Teacher Signals for Reasoning Exploration with Self-Distilled RLVR
papers.description: A privileged-context view of the same model scores tokens in student-sampled rollouts, but its log-probability gap weights a GRPO advantage rather than imposing a distillation KL. Reverse weighting favors student-preferred tokens only on verified successful rollouts; unsuccessful rollouts retain ordinary GRPO. Tests cover mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: On successful rollouts, scale the group-relative GRPO advantage by a clipped reverse student-to-teacher token likelihood ratio; use the ordinary GRPO advantage on unsuccessful rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 11 May 2026]

papers.title: The Many Faces of On-Policy Distillation: Pitfalls, Mechanisms, and Fixes
papers.description: The study tests on-policy distillation across math reasoning, prompt internalization and alignment. It attributes failures to teacher mismatch on student prefixes, biased top-K reverse-KL gradients, and aggregation of instance-specific privileged teachers by a context-free student; its proposed fixes are setting-dependent.
papers.objective: Compares full-vocabulary reverse KL, sampled-token log-ratio policy gradients, and top-K reverse-KL variants, including stop-gradient or renormalized objectives; no single new training loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 11 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 24 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Adaptive Teacher Exposure for Self-Distillation in LLM Reasoning
papers.description: On student-generated reasoning rollouts, a self-teacher sees a controller-chosen prefix of the reference reasoning while retaining the answer, and supplies token targets to the student. A training-state-conditioned controller holds one exposure across multiple updates and learns from delayed progress, not per-example difficulty.
papers.objective: Student-only minimization of token-level forward KL from the exposure-conditioned teacher on student rollouts; the exposure controller uses REINFORCE with delayed learning-progress and teacher-grounded feedback.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 9 Jun 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Anti-Self-Distillation for Reasoning RL via Pointwise Mutual Information
papers.description: For student-sampled reasoning trajectories, this method adds a self-teacher signal to a verifiable-reward policy update, ascending Jensen–Shannon divergence to favor deliberative tokens disfavored by solution-conditioned predictions. Teacher-entropy gating suspends that term when its signal degrades; the induced token advantage is capped only on one side.
papers.objective: A group-normalized sequence-level correctness advantage plus a gated per-token policy-gradient advantage derived from Jensen–Shannon-divergence ascent against a stop-gradient, privileged-context self-teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026]

papers.title: From Generic Correlation to Input-Specific Credit in On-Policy Self Distillation
papers.description: Under a posterior-compatibility assumption, the paper interprets feedback-conditioned self-distillation rewards as filtering increments and subtracts teacher scores for unrelated batch inputs to discount generic response patterns. CREDIT trains on student rollouts, requires extra teacher passes, and its interpretation need not hold without that assumption.
papers.objective: A student-to-stop-gradient-teacher tokenwise reverse-KL update whose vocabulary-level advantages subtract student log probabilities and a batch-contrastive teacher log-probability baseline from feedback-conditioned teacher log probabilities.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026]

papers.title: Learning to Foresee: Unveiling the Unlocking Efficiency of On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This parameter-dynamics study compares where on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning place updates and how early update subspaces align with final directions. An accompanying accelerator validates extrapolations of recent parameter displacements; its studied distillation typically uses a separate stronger teacher, not necessarily a self-teacher.
papers.objective: Analysis of module-level update allocation and directional alignment, with validation-selected parameter extrapolation as an accompanying acceleration update; the underlying distillation loss is unspecified in the supplied excerpts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 21 May 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: GEAR: Granularity-Adaptive Advantage Reweighting for LLM Agents via Self-Distillation
papers.description: GEAR uses divergence from a ground-truth-conditioned self-teacher to start credit regions, entropy to end them, and outcome-dependent weights to redistribute advantage across on-policy agent trajectories. It updates through the reweighted reinforcement-learning objective rather than a distillation loss, and requires suitable ground truth.
papers.objective: Clipped group-relative policy optimization using trajectory outcome advantages reweighted at token or segment level by teacher–student discrepancy; no direct distillation loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 14 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: A Recipe for Long-Context Reasoning in Large Language Models via On-Policy Optimization and Distillation
papers.description: For long-context reasoning, the recipe follows supervised warm-up with student-rollout group-relative optimization that combines outcome rewards and token-level reverse-KL guidance from a stronger teacher. Its synthetic long-context data supports the training pipeline; the distillation term is teacher regularization, not a replacement for reward optimization.
papers.objective: Maximize a clipped group-relative outcome-reward objective while penalizing student-to-teacher token-distribution KL on student-generated rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 10 Sep 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: OGLS-SD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Outcome-Guided Logit Steering for LLM Reasoning
papers.description: OGLS-SD contrasts privileged self-teacher logits conditioned on verified successful and failed on-policy rollouts to steer token-level targets for incorrect student trajectories. Verifiable outcomes construct the target rather than supplying a policy-gradient reward, and steering is skipped when the required outcome pools are unavailable.
papers.objective: Minimize student-to-stop-gradient steered-teacher token KL on incorrect on-policy rollouts; verified outcomes define the contrasting teacher-logit pools.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training
papers.description: This verifiable-math study tests allocating scarce labeled examples first to teacher-side sparse-reward learning, then transferring behavior through a teacher-rollout forward-KL warm-up and student-rollout reverse-KL distillation, with optional later student reinforcement learning. The stages are sequential, not a joint RL–distillation update, and the allocation evidence is task-specific.
papers.objective: Sequential teacher sparse-reward RL, teacher-trajectory forward-KL warm-up, student-trajectory reverse-KL distillation, and optional student sparse-reward RL.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 20 May 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: Multi-Rollout On-Policy Distillation via Peer Successes and Failures
papers.description: For each prompt, the student generates multiple rollouts that a verifier divides into successes and failures. A teacher uses other rollouts from the group to supervise each target rollout through token-level divergence; the approach depends on reliable success labels and available peers.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level divergence between the student and peer-conditioned teacher on student-generated trajectories; reverse KL is used for math tasks and Jensen–Shannon divergence for other tasks.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 1 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Learning with Rare Success but Rich Feedback via Reflection-Enhanced Self-Distillation
papers.description: After a student rollout fails, RESD uses environmental feedback to generate a retrospective diagnosis and curate reusable lessons in a persistent playbook. That context guides a self-teacher’s token-level supervision on student rollouts, including when successful demonstrations are unavailable; it requires informative feedback.
papers.objective: Minimize a clipped, token-level self-distillation divergence between the student and a feedback- and memory-conditioned self-teacher on student-generated rollouts; the divergence choice varies by task.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 May 2026]

papers.title: Revisiting DAgger in the Era of LLM-Agents
papers.description: This DAgger adaptation alternates teacher and student execution at turn boundaries in an interactive agent, then queries teacher actions at visited states and trains the student to imitate those labels. Its states come from mixed-policy trajectories, not exclusively student rollouts; evaluation centers on software-engineering agents.
papers.objective: Cross-entropy on teacher-provided action tokens at states visited during mixed teacher–student environment rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 May 2026]

papers.title: Respecting Self-Uncertainty in On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient LLM Reasoning
papers.description: EGRSD weights student-generated reasoning tokens using outcome-reward advantages, teacher–student likelihood ratios, and an entropy gate with a nonzero floor. Its self-teacher receives a reference solution; a lookahead variant retains transient uncertain pivots, while teacher entropy remains a confidence proxy rather than proof of correctness.
papers.objective: Minimize a policy-gradient-style negative log-likelihood loss on sampled tokens, weighted by a reward-derived advantage, a clipped teacher–student likelihood-ratio magnitude, and a teacher-entropy gate; the weighting terms are stop-gradient.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 May 2026]

papers.title: Reward-Weighted On-Policy Distillation with an Open Property-Equivalence Verifier for NL-to-SVA Generation
papers.description: For natural-language-to-hardware-assertion generation, the student samples candidate assertions, and a property checker retains equivalent or one-way-implying rollouts for reward-weighted, frozen-teacher forward-KL supervision. The checker abstains on unsupported liveness cases, which receive no direct verifier-weighted update.
papers.objective: Truncated teacher-to-student forward KL on student-rollout response tokens, weighted across retained rollouts by property-checker verdict; rejected rollouts contribute no loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 May 2026]

papers.title: Prefix Teach, Suffix Fade: Local Teachability Collapse in Strong-to-Weak On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This study finds that late teacher feedback can lose local discrimination despite a nonzero teacher–student gap. A change point in teacher margins over student candidates masks later advantage-weighted supervision. The rule changes training supervision while preserving complete response generation.
papers.objective: A policy-gradient surrogate weighted by teacher-minus-student sampled-token log-probability advantages, with supervision masked after a sentence-level downward margin change point and retained loss mass rescaled.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 25 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Learning from Language Feedback via Variational Policy Distillation
papers.description: VPD trains a feedback-conditioned teacher view and distills its predictions on collected student trajectories. Its controlled comparisons examine the reference prior and update frequency; those empirical results do not establish the proposed EM monotonicity guarantee.
papers.objective: Feedback-view preference updates followed by student matching; task-specific divergences and reused rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 18 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Self-Distilled Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.description: For multi-turn agents, the method keeps environment-reward policy optimization as the main loss and adds a sigmoid-gated self-distillation term on student trajectories. A skill-conditioned self-teacher’s positive sampled-token probability gaps receive more weight than negative gaps, which may reflect unreliable retrieved skills.
papers.objective: Clipped group-relative policy-gradient loss from environment rewards plus an auxiliary sampled-token teacher–student log-probability-gap term weighted by a detached sigmoid gate.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 May 2026]

papers.title: Reducing the Safety Tax in LLM Safety Alignment with On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: For safety alignment, the student generates responses to harmful and benign prompts while a frozen copy conditioned on type-specific safety or helpfulness context supplies token-distribution targets. Context search uses teacher flip rate; the approach depends on privileged prompts eliciting safer behavior.
papers.objective: Per-token teacher–student distribution matching on student-sampled prefixes, implemented with an equal-weight mixture of forward and reverse KL; the frozen teacher receives type-specific privileged context.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 May 2026]

papers.title: DeltaPrompts: Escaping the Zero-Delta Trap in Multimodal Distillation
papers.description: Measures teacher–student disagreement over sampled final-answer distributions, then synthesizes multimodal questions from dataset seeds and student failure skills while rejecting ambiguous or zero-disagreement candidates. The prompts are evaluated with on-policy distillation and off-policy fine-tuning; answer-level agreement does not establish token-level agreement.
papers.objective: Select prompts using reverse KL between empirical final-answer distributions and teacher-answer consistency; the on-policy distillation evaluation minimizes student-sampled reverse KL to the teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 8 Aug 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Decoupling KL and Trajectories: A Unified Perspective for SFT, DAgger, Offline RL, and OPD in LLM Distillation
papers.description: Compares forward and reverse token-level KL on teacher- or student-generated prefixes, then tests KL mixing and an entropy-gated response-length curriculum. Its tradeoffs are studied chiefly in mathematical reasoning, including initialization for an accuracy-reward RL follow-up, rather than across RL algorithms.
papers.objective: Four token-level objectives cross teacher or student prefixes with forward or reverse KL; forward KL gives soft-target cross-entropy gradients, while reverse KL has a policy-gradient form using a teacher–student log-ratio reward. The proposed extension mixes the two KL losses.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 16 May 2026]

papers.title: Self-Supervised On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning Language Models
papers.description: SSOPD adds frontier-weighted, pointwise-clipped forward KL to verifier-based policy optimization. A fixed self-teacher sees the shortest correct group completion while supervising early prefixes of the longest wrong completion; this auxiliary signal requires a rollout group containing both successes and failures.
papers.objective: A verifier-based group-relative policy loss plus frontier-weighted, pointwise-clipped forward KL from a fixed privileged self-teacher to early prefixes of the longest failed rollout.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 17 May 2026]

papers.title: f-OPD: Stabilizing Long-Horizon On-Policy Distillation with Freshness-Aware Control
papers.description: Analyzes how asynchronous on-policy distillation departs from current-policy training through stale student rollouts and, when teacher context changes, stale supervision. It scores buffered samples for freshness, gates their distillation loss, refreshes the buffer, and penalizes drift from rollout policies; the score is a surrogate, not a guarantee.
papers.objective: Freshness-gated teacher–student distribution matching on buffered prefixes, plus a freshness-gated KL penalty between the current student and the rollout policy; the supplied excerpts do not specify the base matching divergence.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 May 2026]

papers.title: HINT-SD: Targeted Hindsight Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.description: HINT-SD analyzes failed agent rollouts to identify relevant actions and generate local corrections. A hindsight-conditioned self-teacher supervises the student through reverse token KL only at selected action spans; effectiveness depends on feedback that identifies actionable failures.
papers.objective: Minimize student-to-stopped-teacher reverse token KL on selected action spans of failed rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 2 Oct 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: SD-Search: On-Policy Hindsight Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Reasoning
papers.description: SD-Search gives a shared-weight teacher a hindsight summary of the rollout group’s queries and outcomes, then matches its query-token distributions with Jensen–Shannon divergence alongside GRPO. The summary includes the current rollout; outcome contrast weakens when every rollout succeeds or fails.
papers.objective: Add token-level Jensen–Shannon divergence at search-query positions to a GRPO loss based on trajectory-level answer rewards.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 May 2026]

papers.title: AMR-SD: Asymmetric Meta-Reflective Self-Distillation for Token-Level Credit Assignment
papers.description: AMR-SD turns rollout diagnostics into hints or critiques for a self-teacher, then uses thresholded teacher–student log-probability differences to amplify outcome-based token advantages. The modulation decays during training; negative-advantage rollouts without successful peers fall back to the base policy objective.
papers.objective: A clipped policy-gradient objective with outcome-based advantages amplified by thresholded, asymmetric teacher-minus-student sampled-token log-probability differences; amplification is annealed to zero.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 May 2026]

papers.title: Vision-OPD: Learning to See Fine Details for Multimodal LLMs via On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: A full-image student generates responses while a crop-conditioned self-teacher scores the same prefixes, and training minimizes token-level Jensen–Shannon divergence through the student alone. The method requires paired evidence-centered crops and fine-grained questions prepared for training, rather than discovering target regions at inference.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level Jensen–Shannon divergence between crop-conditioned teacher and full-image student distributions on student-generated prefixes, with gradients through the student only.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 2 Jun 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: It Takes Two: Complementary Self-Distillation for Contextual Integrity in LLMs
papers.description: On student-generated responses, two feedback-conditioned self-teachers separately guide task-relevant retention and minimal disclosure through weighted token-level reverse KL, inducing a product-of-experts target. The construction uses explicit attribute partitions and synthetic disclosure decisions, and evaluation focuses on final responses.
papers.objective: Weighted sum of two token-level reverse-KL losses from the student to stopped utility- and privacy-oriented self-teacher distributions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 May 2026]

papers.title: AVSD: Adaptive-View Self-Distillation by Balancing Consensus and Teacher-Specific Privileged Signals
papers.description: AVSD combines privileged views of the same model on student-generated trajectories. A geometric consensus anchors the target, while gated view-specific residuals adjust it; the student learns through reverse KL. Evaluation covers mathematical and code reasoning, with broader agent applications left untested.
papers.objective: Token-level reverse KL from the student to a stopped target reconstructed from geometric cross-view consensus and gated residual support.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 May 2026]

papers.title: When Are Teacher Tokens Reliable? Position-Weighted On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
papers.description: PW-OPSD increases position weights on clipped forward-KL supervision from a privileged-answer self-teacher and averages losses per sequence. Its reliability diagnostic concerns ambiguous candidate tokens on correct reasoning traces; the reported method changes both weighting and aggregation, limiting attribution to weighting alone.
papers.objective: Position-weighted, per-sequence mean of vocabulary-wise clipped forward-KL terms from a privileged-answer self-teacher to the student on student-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 May 2026]

papers.title: On-Policy Consistency Training Improves LLM Safety with Minimal Capability Degradation
papers.description: A frozen copy of the initial model scores current student responses under clean or safety-fact-augmented prompts, while the student samples under perturbed or unaugmented prompts and learns from sampled-token likelihood ratios. Its scope depends on the teacher eliciting appropriate behavior in these safety settings.
papers.objective: Sampled-token student-minus-frozen-teacher log-likelihood ratios on student rollouts under paired contrastive prompts, used to estimate a reverse-KL objective.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 May 2026]

papers.title: Visual-Advantage On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
papers.description: On student-generated vision-language rollouts, a teacher compares token probabilities with intact and degraded images to estimate sensitivity to fine visual detail. The method reweights sibling rollouts and separately averages reverse KL over high- and low-sensitivity tokens; sensitivity is a proxy, not a direct measure of perception.
papers.objective: Trajectory-averaged visual advantage weights sibling rollouts; within each rollout, weighted averages of student-to-teacher token KL for high- and low-advantage groups form the loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 21 May 2026]

papers.title: Unlocking Proactivity in Task-Oriented Dialogue
papers.description: For simulated multi-turn recruitment dialogues, a privileged view of the policy sees hidden user concerns and supplies token-level targets to its conversation-only view on the latter’s rollouts. A separate clipped policy-gradient update uses simulated final decisions and turn-level willingness shifts; deployment has no access to the hidden concerns.
papers.objective: Turn-weighted teacher-to-student token KL with a stop-gradient privileged self-teacher, plus a clipped policy-gradient loss whose advantages use final decisions and per-turn willingness shifts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 21 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Tailoring Teaching to Aptitude: Direction-Adaptive Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
papers.description: On student-generated reasoning rollouts, entropy determines whether a privileged self-teacher’s sampled-token signal attracts or repels the student: low-entropy positions receive attraction and high-entropy positions repulsion. A verifier supplies the trajectory-level outcome signal, so the implemented update is a clipped policy-gradient surrogate rather than a standalone KL loss.
papers.objective: A clipped policy-gradient surrogate uses verifier-based trajectory advantages augmented by a normalized, entropy-signed sampled-token log-probability gap against a stop-gradient privileged self-teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 21 May 2026]

papers.title: Not All Disagreement Is Learnable: Token Teachability in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: A fixed-context diagnostic tests whether teacher–student disagreement predicts local KL reduction, separating teacher corrections on the student’s top candidates from largely off-support disagreement. The resulting selector applies reverse-KL distillation only at high-teachability positions on student rollouts; teachability measures local compatibility, not teacher reliability or answer-level success.
papers.objective: A binary position mask retains high-scoring support-aligned disagreement for student-to-teacher reverse-KL distillation; teacher-to-student KL reduction on frozen prefixes is diagnostic, not the training loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 May 2026]

papers.title: Less is More: Early Stopping Rollout for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Early Stopping Rollout truncates student-generated responses at a fixed token position and applies teacher-scored reverse-KL distillation only to that prefix, addressing deterioration of teacher feedback on later student-conditioned tokens. Its experiments start with students that already have basic reasoning ability.
papers.objective: Reverse KL from student to teacher token distributions, evaluated on student-generated prefixes up to a fixed cutoff.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 May 2026]

papers.title: Counteraction-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for General Capability Recovery with Domain Preservation
papers.description: CaMOPD alternates general-capability recovery and domain-preservation updates on student rollouts. It selects recovery samples by absolute teacher–student log-probability gaps and preservation samples by positive gaps; experiments use proxy general prompts and cover role-play dialogue and medical reasoning.
papers.objective: An importance-weighted policy-gradient loss using stop-gradient, token-level teacher–student log-probability gaps as feedback; selected samples receive branch-specific scaling.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 14 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: MAIGO: Mitigating Lost-in-Conversation with History-Cleaned On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: MAIGO trains on the student's self-conditioned, multi-turn dialogue rollouts while an EMA self-reference scores middle replies without prior assistant messages and final answers using the completed user-side task view. A separate full-view branch preserves complete-prompt behavior; evaluation is limited to paired-view tasks.
papers.objective: Token-distribution matching on student-sampled replies: symmetric Jensen–Shannon loss with reliability weighting for middle turns, reverse KL for answer and full-view branches; gradients pass only through the student.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 30 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Pair-In, Pair-Out: Latent Multi-Token Prediction for Efficient LLMs
papers.description: PIPO combines paired-token latent input compression with multi-token prediction and learns a confidence head from teacher-to-student acceptance probabilities during on-policy distillation. The head replaces inference-time verifier passes; experiments cover pairwise compression on the tested Qwen3.5 backbones.
papers.objective: On-policy sampled-token reverse-KL distillation for backbone and draft positions, plus binary cross-entropy for confidence against detached teacher-to-student draft acceptance probabilities; an earlier supervised stage uses token cross-entropy.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Beyond Imitation: Reflective On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
papers.description: A self-reflector compares incorrect on-policy rollouts with successful ones to supply a corrective idea and locate the first error. The idea conditions a self-teacher, while distillation skips the valid prefix; correct rollouts and unmatched error quotes receive full-response supervision.
papers.objective: Token-level Jensen–Shannon distillation from a reflection-conditioned, stop-gradient self-teacher on student rollouts, masked before the located error for incorrect rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 28 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Skill-Conditioned Gated Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
papers.description: The student samples from a plain problem prompt while skill-and-mistake-conditioned self-teachers score that same rollout. Verifier outcomes determine whether each teacher’s support should be followed, reversed, or ignored; a gated sampled-token loss limits weak and extreme disagreements rather than assuming retrieved skills are trustworthy.
papers.objective: Retrieval-weighted, outcome-polarity-signed gated loss on sampled-token teacher–student log-probability gaps, with masked positions and stop-gradient teachers; not a direct token-KL loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Sep 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: GAPD: Gold-Action Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning in Knowledge Base Question Answering
papers.description: For knowledge-base question answering, GAPD aligns student and gold execution states through reached entity sets. A self-teacher conditioned on the matched gold action supplies token guidance alongside outcome-based reinforcement learning; turns without an accepted state match receive no gold-action guidance.
papers.objective: A GRPO-style clipped policy-gradient loss using final-outcome advantages fused with teacher–student sampled-token log-probability guidance on aligned action spans.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Same Evidence, Different Answers: Canonical-Context On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Language Models
papers.description: CCOPD trains a student answering from a multi-turn history against a frozen copy of the same base model given the same user evidence in a clean prompt. Reverse KL aligns student-generated final-answer prefixes; earlier conversational replies receive no direct distillation loss.
papers.objective: Final-answer-masked reverse KL between the history-conditioned student and frozen full-context teacher at the student’s sampled answer prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 May 2026]

papers.title: Your Teacher Can't Help You Here: Combating Supervision Fidelity Decay in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: On student-generated reasoning prefixes, this method addresses declining teacher confidence by rewarding candidate tokens that leave the teacher more confident at the next position, alongside reverse-KL distillation. The extra signal is gated by student entropy and requires access to teacher logits.
papers.objective: Per-token reverse-KL teacher feedback plus a group-normalized, one-step teacher-confidence reward at high-student-entropy positions; reverse KL alone elsewhere.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 May 2026]

papers.title: Trust-Region Behavior Blending for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: During warmup, a teacher-guided sampling policy stays within a student-centered KL trust region to collect prefixes, while the student retains its per-prefix reverse-KL update. The budget decays to student-only rollouts; online teacher decoding adds warmup overhead.
papers.objective: Minimize per-prefix student-to-teacher reverse KL on collected prefixes, estimated on truncated student top-k support; during warmup, choose a behavior policy closest to the teacher subject to a KL-to-student budget.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 May 2026]

papers.title: Are Full Rollouts Necessary for On-Policy Distillation?
papers.description: This study varies how much of each student-generated rollout receives token-level teacher feedback: one strategy gradually lengthens the training horizon, while another keeps it truncated. Its reasoning results concern training on partial rollouts; evaluation still permits full-length generation.
papers.objective: Token-level teacher-versus-student log-ratio feedback on generated tokens, without accumulating future-token signals; generation and distillation stop at a progressively expanded or fixed truncated horizon.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 1 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: RAFT: Data Refinement and Adaptive Distillation for Domain Fine-Tuning with Alleviated Forgetting
papers.description: For domain fine-tuning, this pipeline refines answer data before combining supervised learning with distillation on student-generated responses. The original model supplies soft targets using privileged fused-answer context, with adaptive loss balancing; the studied scope is domain adaptation and retention of general capabilities.
papers.objective: Cross-entropy on refined domain answers plus an adaptively weighted teacher-to-student KL loss on student-generated trajectories, using temperature-scaled distributions renormalized over teacher-selected top-K tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 May 2026]

papers.title: Bridging Reasoning Trajectories in On-Policy Distillation via Near-Future Guidance
papers.description: TOPD compares short teacher and student continuations from the same student prefix to identify consequential divergence, then adds optimal-transport-aligned guidance across future tokens to ordinary distillation. Its correction uses a short future window and requires additional teacher and student continuations.
papers.objective: Token-level on-policy reverse-KL loss plus a weighted teacher-to-student KL loss against optimal-transport-aligned soft targets at selected future positions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Weak Critics Make Strong Learners: On-Policy Critique Distillation for Scalable Oversight
papers.description: A weak model critiques the strong model’s sampled answers; outcome and rubric checks select critiques before a critique-conditioned copy of the strong model supplies token distributions to its unconditioned student. Training refreshes answers and critiques, although its procedure also retains earlier selected examples.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level KL from the unconditioned student distribution to a stopped-gradient, critique-conditioned self-teacher distribution on selected answer trajectories.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 21 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Decomposed On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Reasoning: Steering Gradients for Visual Grounding
papers.description: For vision-language OPD, this work separates language-prior matching from visual grounding and examines their gradient directions. Its update adds visual-target distillation to standard reverse KL, with selective language preservation; the visual signal depends on differences between the teacher’s image-conditioned and text-only predictions.
papers.objective: Minimize reverse KL on student-sampled multimodal trajectories, augmented by reverse KL to a constructed visual target and selective text-only language-prior KL.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 30 May 2026]

papers.title: OPD+: Rethinking the Advantage Design for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: OPD+ studies policy-gradient coefficients for student-sampled, single-token estimates of teacher–student f-divergences and restores the omitted direct dependence of divergence feedback on the student. For reverse KL the correction is a constant baseline in expectation; this immediate-token analysis does not by itself settle full-trajectory credit.
papers.objective: Minimize an f-divergence between next-token distributions on student-sampled prefixes using an immediate-token policy-gradient coefficient corrected for the student-dependent feedback.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 31 May 2026]

papers.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: TrOPD classifies student-generated tokens by teacher–student decoding agreement, using sampled reverse-KL supervision in the trust region and top-k forward-KL guidance for outliers. It also imitates teacher-generated prefixes before student continuations, annealing those prefixes away during training.
papers.objective: Sampled reverse-KL supervision for trusted student tokens, top-k forward-KL loss for outlier tokens, and forward-KL imitation on teacher-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 31 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 17 Jun 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: CoMAP: Co-Evolving World Models and Agent Policies for LLM Agents
papers.description: COMAP uses a textual world model’s predicted next state to help an agent decide whether to revise a draft action. Executed transitions then train the world model with observed-state supervision and on-policy self-distillation from a privileged teacher mode; the setting assumes text-representable states and outcomes.
papers.objective: World-model next-state likelihood plus token-level divergence from a stop-gradient, observed-state-conditioned teacher on student-generated next-state sequences; separate supervised action-refinement and refinement-gate losses train the policy.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 1 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment
papers.description: SafeSteer builds a refusal-oriented self-teacher by activation steering, then votes on teacher–base-model probability contrasts to select safety-related vocabulary items. On student-generated responses to harmful prompts, it applies reverse-KL loss only over those items, rather than restricting generation or scoring to them.
papers.objective: Reverse-KL sum over unnormalized probability slices for a selected safety vocabulary subset, averaged across positions in student-generated responses to harmful prompts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 1 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 21 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Filter, Then Reweight: Rethinking Optimization Granularity in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: FiRe-OPD discards student-generated trajectories with low average teacher likelihood, then softly reweights token updates in retained trajectories using teacher confidence and student uncertainty. Its PPO-style clipped update uses teacher–old-policy token log-likelihood differences; the filtering does not avoid generating the discarded trajectories.
papers.objective: PPO-style clipped policy-gradient loss with a teacher-versus-old-policy token log-likelihood advantage, normalized soft token weights, and exclusion of low-teacher-likelihood trajectories.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 1 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 4 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Constitutional On-Policy Safe Distillation
papers.description: COPSD calibrates a constitution-conditioned teacher with Cross-SFT before distilling on student-generated responses. Same-data teacher comparisons and calibration-data ablations examine the resulting safety–utility tradeoff; the proposed geometric explanation remains separate from this empirical evidence.
papers.objective: Teacher calibration followed by token log-ratio policy updates; an optional variant also uses outcome reward.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 13 Aug 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: When Should the Teacher Move? Temporal Coupling and Stability in Self On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: The paper studies freezing and refreshing a historical self-teacher, then proposes hard refreshes gated by a minimum isolation period, reward improvement, and response-length tail safety. Its stability findings are empirical and confined to the evaluated model and task settings.
papers.objective: A group-relative reward policy-gradient loss plus teacher distillation approximated by top-k Jensen–Shannon divergence with importance-sampling correction.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Jun 2026]

papers.title: World Models Meet Language Models: On the Complementarity of Concrete and Abstract Reasoning
papers.description: PF-OPSD trains a student to invoke, check, and use world-model simulations for visual future prediction. A privileged evaluator scores student trajectories using true future videos and answers; those scores supervise decisions and text, while the evaluator and true futures remain unavailable at deployment.
papers.objective: Privileged-evaluator scores produce advantage-weighted discrete-action KL targets and weighted text log-likelihood, alongside protocol supervision and a simulation-call penalty.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 31 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Self-Distilled Policy Gradient
papers.description: SDPG combines group-normalized verifier advantages with full-vocabulary reverse-KL self-distillation on student prefixes, using a detached, privileged-context branch of the same model. Distillation is gated to positive-advantage rollouts and accompanied by fixed-reference regularization; its policy-gradient identity applies locally at a sampled prefix.
papers.objective: A group-relative verifier policy-gradient loss plus positive-advantage-gated, full-vocabulary student-to-detached-teacher reverse KL and fixed-reference KL regularization.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Jun 2026]

papers.title: DuDi: Dual-Signal Distillation with Cross-Lingual Verbalizer
papers.description: DuDi combines live comparisons between ground-truth and student-generated responses with token distillation on both corpus responses and student rollouts. A cross-lingual demonstration prompt conditions the teacher’s token feedback; the evaluated multilingual setup does not establish a mapping between heterogeneous tokenizers.
papers.objective: A SPIN-style logistic contrast between ground-truth and student-generated responses, plus off-policy and on-policy token-distribution distillation; the cross-lingual on-policy term uses a demonstration-conditioned teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 10 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Rethinking Continual Experience Internalization for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
papers.description: This study asks whether repeated internalization of experience-aware behavior sustains gains in web agents, comparing experience granularity, injection timing, and trajectory source. In its tested setting, filtered teacher trajectories provide more stable training than repeated distillation on student-induced states.
papers.objective: Compare forward KL matching on teacher-generated trajectories with reverse KL matching on student-generated trajectories, using an experience-conditioned teacher and an experience-free student.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Self-Evaluation Is Already There: Eliciting Latent Judge Calibration in Base LLMs with Minimal Data
papers.description: SEE alternates reinforcement learning from external-judge quality and calibration rewards with masked training on collected model responses, replacing their self-ratings with the judge’s scores. The masked loss supervises self-evaluation score tokens, not answer tokens or a judge’s token distribution.
papers.objective: Optimize the full response with a reward combining judge-rated answer quality and agreement between self-scores and judge scores; then apply masked cross-entropy to judge-score tokens in reused rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 28 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning from Rich Feedback with Distributional DAgger
papers.description: DistIL queries a feedback-conditioned expert at prefixes visited by the student and minimizes forward cross-entropy, retaining a gradient term that credits earlier decisions for later disagreement. Its monotonic-improvement result concerns a better teacher and an idealized local update under stated assumptions.
papers.objective: Teacher-weighted forward cross-entropy on student-visited prefixes, optimized with both local imitation gradients and a policy-gradient term carrying future cross-entropy back to earlier actions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 5 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Data-Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Models via On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: A converted diffusion student samples its own reverse-denoising trajectory, then matches the frozen source autoregressive model’s token distributions at masked positions using causal prefixes from the completed student sequence. This addresses diffusion inference states, not ordinary autoregressive prefixes or agent turns.
papers.objective: Teacher-to-student token-distribution KL at masked positions in a sampled student reverse-denoising state.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Teaching the Way, Not the Answer: Privileged Tutoring Distillation for Multimodal Policy Optimization
papers.description: For multimodal reasoning with verifiable rewards, a frozen, hint-conditioned self-teacher guides failed student rollouts through token-distribution matching while the student sees only the original question. Spatial and intermediate reasoning hints are prepared offline using answers, but are intended not to reveal them.
papers.objective: Group-relative optimization from verifiable rewards plus failure-gated Jensen–Shannon matching of teacher and student token distributions, approximated on combined top-token support with a tail bucket.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Jun 2026]

papers.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This parameter-space study compares distillation updates with supervised fine-tuning and verifiable-reward reinforcement learning, finding early low-dimensional subspace locking and an intermediate off-principal update pattern. Token sparsification and off-policy rollout controls preserve rank dynamics, so locking is not isolated to on-policy sampling.
papers.objective: Analyzes sampled-token student–teacher log-probability-gap corrections in policy-gradient updates, alongside supervised cross-entropy and verifiable-reward updates.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 14 Jun 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Trajectory-Refined Distillation
papers.description: A student first generates a rollout, which a teacher refines using that rollout and a reference solution; distillation then matches token distributions along the refined trajectory rather than the original student prefixes. Teacher-generated corrections change the supervised state distribution, so this is not pure direct on-policy matching.
papers.objective: Full-vocabulary teacher-to-student token-distribution KL along teacher-refined trajectories seeded by student rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Thinking Without Images: Internalizing Visual Manipulation with On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: A student generates textual visual-inspection traces from the original image, while a fixed self-teacher scores the same prefixes with annotated-region crops and the answer. Token-level reverse-KL training transfers that guidance without test-time crops; training requires region annotations.
papers.objective: Average token-level reverse KL from the student distribution to the privileged teacher distribution on student-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Jun 2026]

papers.title: PBSD: Privileged Bayesian Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Credit Assignment
papers.description: For multi-turn search agents, PBSD compares each sampled turn’s likelihood under an answer-conditioned self-teacher and the ordinary student. The resulting evidence score reweights outcome-based policy advantages rather than making the student imitate teacher tokens; it requires verified final answers.
papers.objective: Outcome-reward policy optimization with turn-level advantages reweighted by detached, answer-conditioned teacher-versus-student log-likelihood contrasts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 6 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Breaking the Tokenizer Barrier: On-Policy Distillation across Model Families
papers.description: Cross-tokenizer OPD aligns student rollouts and teacher retokenizations into minimal matching text chunks, then allocates teacher chunk log-likelihood across student tokens using their prior log-probabilities. The resulting advantages drive clipped policy updates; supervision relies on aligned text chunks rather than shared vocabulary coordinates.
papers.objective: Clipped importance-sampling policy objective using student-token advantages allocated from aligned teacher chunk log-likelihoods.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Escaping the KL Agreement Trap in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: KAT examines whether teacher–student reverse KL stays low across consecutive regions of a student rollout, which can signal weak supervision after a degraded prefix. It terminates such rollouts using a training-adaptive threshold while retaining the OPD loss; evaluation focuses on mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: Standard token-level reverse-KL OPD on the retained student rollout prefix; persistent low-KL agreement determines online termination, not a new loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Self-Distillation Policy Optimization via Visual Feedback: Bridging Code and Visual Artifacts
papers.description: On student-generated code for charts, interfaces, and slides, a weight-sharing teacher re-scores tokens with rendered feedback. Defect-to-statement mapping weights token-level KL alongside a sequence-level reward; failed executions instead supply error traces to the teacher.
papers.objective: Statement-weighted token-level student-to-teacher KL on student rollouts, jointly with a sequence-level GRPO objective using execution success and visual-quality reward.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Beyond Absolute Imitation: Anchored Residual Guidance for Privileged On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: On student-generated reasoning prefixes, a teacher given part of a privileged trace supplies an anchor, while a scaled log-probability residual adds guidance from the full trace. Forward-KL distillation trains the context-free student; residual strength is fixed rather than gated by token uncertainty.
papers.objective: Token-level forward KL from a normalized partial-privilege anchor plus a scaled full-minus-partial log-probability residual to the student, on student-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Jun 2026]

papers.title: HERO: Hindsight-Enhanced Reflection from Environment Observations for Agentic Self-Distillation
papers.description: For multi-turn tool use, a reflector converts completed student interactions into turn-specific diagnoses. A self-teacher sees the original decision context, next observation, outcome and diagnosis before re-scoring original action tokens; distillation covers only turns with nonempty parsed hints.
papers.objective: Generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence between student and stop-gradient self-teacher token distributions on original assistant actions, restricted to turns with nonempty parsed reflection hints.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Jun 2026]

papers.title: When Context Returns: Toward Robust Internalization in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: After on-policy context distillation, reintroducing privileged context can worsen a student's answers. No-Context Anchoring adds a forward-KL consistency loss that treats the student's no-context output as a stop-gradient target for its context-conditioned output on reused student rollouts; it does not guarantee invariance.
papers.objective: Token-level no-context-student-to-privileged-teacher KL plus forward KL from the stop-gradient no-context student distribution to its context-conditioned distribution, using the same no-context student rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 4 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: RLCSD: Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: RLCSD contrasts a self-teacher conditioned on correct versus incorrect same-query rollouts to reduce hint-induced style drift in sampled-token guidance. It uses that guidance to modulate a verifier-derived advantage in a clipped policy update, rather than directly minimizing contrastive reverse KL.
papers.objective: A two-path clipped policy loss: a bounded correct-minus-incorrect hint signal modulates the verifier-derived advantage without reversing its sign, alongside an unmodulated path.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 14 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation: Post-Training Without Rubric Verifiers
papers.description: RGSD trains on student-generated responses by matching a prompt-only student to a frozen copy of its base policy given the prompt-specific rubric. It uses clipped Jensen–Shannon token-distribution loss without a training-time judge; rubric-conditioned teaching depends on the base model responding meaningfully to rubrics.
papers.objective: Minimize clipped Jensen–Shannon divergence between student and frozen rubric-conditioned teacher token distributions at student-visited prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates: On the Sparsity and Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This analysis measures checkpoint updates after on-policy distillation, finding coordinate-sparse changes distributed across modules and numerically full-rank matrices with concentrated spectra. The visible changes favor low-magnitude, nonprincipal source coordinates; these are observations across studied model pairs, not a new training objective.
papers.objective: Analyze checkpoint-delta sparsity, module distribution, singular spectra, and overlap with source-weight coordinate masks; test training restricted to the discovered update support.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 11 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 30 Jul 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Be My Tutor: On-Policy Co-Distillation for Mutual LLM Improvement via Peer Feedback
papers.description: OPCoD alternates two domain specialists as tutors and students: each matches a self-teacher conditioned on its own correct rollout, when available, and gated peer feedback. A problem-based anchor filters ungrounded feedback; reported mutual improvement is limited to the evaluated science-domain pairs.
papers.objective: Minimize token-distribution divergence on each student's sampled responses against its feedback-conditioned self-teacher, using Jensen–Shannon divergence in the reported implementation.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Jun 2026]

papers.title: PowerOPD: Stabilizing On-Policy Distillation with Bounded Power Transformation
papers.description: PowerOPD replaces the detached teacher–student log-ratio coefficient on student-sampled tokens with a bounded, sign-preserving difference of powered token probabilities in a policy-gradient update. Its evaluations focus on mathematical reasoning and a limited set of teacher–student pairs.
papers.objective: A policy-gradient update on student rollouts, weighted at each sampled token by the stopped difference between powered teacher and student probabilities; this is not an exact reverse-KL update.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Rethinking Reward Supervision: Rubric-Conditioned Self-Distillation
papers.description: This two-stage self-distillation pipeline first learns question-specific rubrics, then conditions a privileged teacher on them to guide the student at its own generated prefixes. The reasoner uses token-level forward KL rather than a scalar rubric reward; evaluation emphasizes scientific reasoning.
papers.objective: Token-level forward KL from the rubric-conditioned teacher distribution to the student distribution along student-generated answer trajectories.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 17 Jun 2026]

papers.title: AsyncOPD: How Stale Can On-Policy Distillation Be?
papers.description: AsyncOPD studies stale student rollouts when teacher scores are cached for limited token sets, then overlaps rollout, teacher scoring and learning. For reverse-KL updates it refreshes the student-dependent advantage and averages importance-weighted local token samples; this addresses sampled actions at fixed prefixes, not stale prefixes.
papers.objective: A local reverse-KL policy-gradient surrogate averaging old-to-current importance-weighted token samples with learner-time, stopped teacher–student log-ratio advantages; forward-KL staleness is analyzed separately.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 23 Jun 2026]

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Sampled Demonstrations Reduces Output Diversity
papers.description: This analysis asks whether self-distillation conditioned on sampled correct demonstrations narrows solution coverage. A fixed-base-teacher derivation shows how expected reverse-KL targets can favor demonstration-aligned correct paths; graph and science-question experiments examine reduced functional and semantic diversity, rather than proposing a new update.
papers.objective: Analyzes expected token-level reverse KL from the student to a stopped, demonstration-conditioned teacher on student rollouts; the sequence-level theoretical optimum additionally includes KL regularization to the base policy.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 24 Jun 2026]

papers.title: ATOD: Annealed Turn-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agentic Tasks
papers.description: For multi-turn agents, ATOD samples student environment trajectories and uses a clipped policy-gradient update whose detached teacher log-probability gap is annealed against an outcome-reward advantage. Disagreement and sampled-token uncertainty weight only the teacher term by turn, not the rewards.
papers.objective: A clipped policy-gradient surrogate using an annealed sum of a detached, turn-weighted teacher-versus-student token log-probability gap and a group-relative outcome-reward advantage.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 10 Aug 2026 (this version, v6)]

papers.title: SEAD: Competence-Aware On-Policy Distillation via Entropy-Guided Supervision
papers.description: SEAD trains on student rollouts scored by a teacher, routing tokens by joint entropy to no update, reverse KL, or forward KL. It reduces the forward-KL branch over training and orders math prompts by initial student pass rate; difficulty scores are not refreshed.
papers.objective: Reverse KL on teacher-confident, student-uncertain tokens; a scheduled, diminishing forward-KL term on teacher-uncertain tokens; and zero gradient on skipped tokens, using an easy-to-hard prompt curriculum.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 Jun 2026]

papers.title: UCOB: Learning to Utilize and Evolve Agentic Skills via Credit-Aware On-Policy Bidirectional Self-Distillation
papers.description: UCOB collects skill-conditioned and unconditioned on-policy agent rollouts, compares return-to-go at matched task and anchor states, and distills the higher-return view’s stopped token distribution into the other alongside RL. The teacher direction can reverse; comparisons depend on matching states.
papers.objective: Return-gap-weighted, confidence-gated top-token-support KL from the higher-return context view to the other view, as auxiliary supervision alongside online RL and skill-writer training.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 17 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: KbSD: Knowledge Boundary aware Self-Distillation for Behavioral Calibration in Agentic Search
papers.description: For agentic search, KbSD uses a boundary-hinted self-teacher to supervise a hint-free student, selecting reverse matching on student rollouts, teacher-trajectory likelihood, or a gradient-balanced combination by knowledge quadrant alongside reward optimization. Its teacher-generated forward examples are not student-state OPD.
papers.objective: Quadrant-selected reverse KL on student rollouts, teacher-trajectory likelihood for the forward branch, or a gradient-balanced combination, jointly with group-relative reward policy optimization and reference-policy KL regularization.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Building Multi-Task Agentic LLMs via Two-Phase Distillation
papers.description: The method first fits a shared student to pooled trajectories from task-specific reinforcement-learning experts, then refines it on student-generated trajectories scored by the matching expert. The first phase provides initialization for the second, which requires the student to generate useful trajectories.
papers.objective: Negative log likelihood on expert-generated trajectories, followed by reverse-KL-targeting policy-gradient updates on student samples using per-token teacher-minus-student log probabilities as advantages.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Jun 2026]

papers.title: DRIFT: Difficulty Routing Self-DIstillation with Rhythm-Gated Exploration and Success BuFfer Training
papers.description: DRIFT warms up with self-distillation, then applies privileged-sibling token distillation to failed student rollouts and difficulty-weighted, rhythm-gated policy updates to successful ones. A historical success buffer supplies sibling context when the current group has no success, so teacher context is not always newly sampled.
papers.objective: Stop-gradient Jensen–Shannon distillation from a success-conditioned self-teacher on incorrect rollouts; clipped group-relative policy-gradient updates on correct rollouts, weighted by problem difficulty and token-level rhythm gating.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 10 Aug 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
papers.description: After independently training domain specialists from a shared checkpoint, MOPD routes each student-generated trajectory to its matching frozen teacher for token-level supervision. It studies clipped sampled-token policy-gradient and corrected top-token distillation implementations; its teacher-replacement experiment shows a limitation when teacher and student distributions differ.
papers.objective: Per-token student-to-routed-teacher reverse KL on student rollouts, implemented either with a clipped sampled-token policy-gradient estimator or a bias-corrected, teacher-top-token truncated loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Regime-Aware Peer Specialization for Robust RAG under Heterogeneous Knowledge Conflicts
papers.description: RAPS-DA routes student rollouts by the training-time reliability regime of retrieved context to same-scale peer teachers, then masks and reweights token-level reverse-KL supervision while shifting toward harder tokens. Regime labels and peers are not needed at deployment; the study concerns knowledge conflicts in retrieval-augmented generation.
papers.objective: Regime-routed, top-token truncated student-to-peer reverse KL on student rollouts, with token eligibility masks, correction weights, and difficulty-annealed token retention.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Jun 2026]

papers.title: DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation
papers.description: DOPD supervises student-sampled trajectories by routing each token between a privileged teacher and a privileged student, using their advantage gap and relative probabilities to vary supervision strength and form. Its routing depends on the availability and quality of privileged information.
papers.objective: Token-routed distillation: strong full-vocabulary teacher matching for credible capability advantages, lighter teacher matching or weak privileged-student regularization elsewhere.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Behavior Cloning is Not All You Need: The Optimality of On-Policy Distillation for Noisy Expert Feedback
papers.description: This analysis asks why learner-state queries can outperform offline cloning when expert feedback is noisy. It derives an offline horizon barrier and studies interactive imitation through augmented-trajectory matching; its guarantees depend on a finite policy class and corruption assumptions, not on arbitrary OPD procedures.
papers.objective: For the practical on-policy variants, minimize forward or reverse KL between noisy-expert and student action distributions on learner-visited prefixes; the theoretical aggregation algorithm instead uses trajectory-level negative log-likelihood of queried expert actions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Jun 2026]

papers.title: Reward-Gated On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: RG-OPD samples student trajectories and uses verifier feedback together with the teacher–student trajectory likelihood gap to admit or discard each trajectory. It applies token-level reverse-KL distillation only to admitted trajectories; verifier reward gates supervision rather than supplying a separate reward-maximization loss.
papers.objective: Minimize top-k-approximated student-to-teacher reverse KL on student-visited states, restricted to trajectories whose verifier advantage and teacher–student likelihood gap agree in direction.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Jul 2026]

papers.title: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
papers.description: UI-MOPD trains a shared GUI student on its own rollouts, routing each desktop or mobile trajectory to the corresponding platform specialist. Teacher guidance preserves platform-specific behavior during adaptation; the reported evidence concerns the evaluated desktop and mobile environments.
papers.objective: Student-rollout distillation from the platform-selected teacher; the local v1 combines clipped policy optimization with an adaptively masked teacher divergence, while the current v2 abstract does not specify the complete loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 10 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: dOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Diffusion Language Models
papers.description: For diffusion language models, dOPSD matches predictions at masked positions in a student decoding state to stop-gradient predictions from later states of the same trajectory. Its reported training keeps only final-answer-correct rollouts; the teacher’s extra context does not come from a reference solution.
papers.objective: Correctness-gated, token-level generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence between current-state student predictions and averaged later-state teacher predictions, with gradients only through the student.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Trust Region Policy Distillation
papers.description: TOP-D interpolates an external teacher’s token probabilities with the rollout student’s to lower-bound the negative log-ratio reward, then uses clipped trust-region updates to reuse student-generated batches. Its gradient-variance analysis concerns autoregressive generation and assumes bounded score-function gradients and a finite vocabulary.
papers.objective: Maximize a clipped policy-gradient objective with normalized token advantages derived from the proximal-teacher-to-student log-ratio reward and future returns.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation with Prefix Replay
papers.description: ReOPD samples earlier turns more often from recorded teacher interaction histories, has the student generate an action at the selected turn, and matches teacher token distributions there. The action is student-generated, but its preceding actions and tool observations are replayed, not student-on-policy.
papers.objective: Minimize per-token reverse KL from the student to the teacher along a student-generated action after a replayed teacher prefix; select prefix positions with a step-decaying sampling schedule.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Jul 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Direct-OPD uses the log-likelihood shift between a teacher’s pre- and post-RL checkpoints as an implicit reward on student-generated prefixes, with a separate KL anchor to the student’s initialization. Its local update restricts actions to student-selected candidates; teacher feedback can become unreliable on later prefixes.
papers.objective: Maximize the pre-/post-RL teacher checkpoint log-likelihood shift on student rollouts, regularized by KL from the updated student to its initialization; the local surrogate uses detached student probabilities over student-selected top-k actions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 8 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: TurnOPD: Making On-Policy Distillation Turn-Aware for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Training
papers.description: TurnOPD collects student-generated agent trajectories to a depth chosen from periodic turn-level probes, then gradually shifts reverse-KL supervision from token-weighted to turn-balanced aggregation. It addresses shallow-turn loss concentration in long-horizon tasks; shortened rollouts can leave deeper decisions unobserved.
papers.objective: Reverse KL from student to teacher on response tokens at student-visited states, with trajectory-normalized and turn-normalized token weights progressively blended.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 28 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Geometric Self-Distillation for Reasoning Generalization
papers.description: GeoSD matches a privileged-context self-teacher on student-generated reasoning prefixes using a Hellinger loss that weakens low-overlap teacher preferences. A Fisher–Rao penalty to a recent checkpoint and a natural-gradient update regulate predictive movement; evaluation is on mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: Mean Hellinger loss between student and stop-gradient privileged-context teacher next-token distributions on student rollouts, plus a squared Fisher–Rao distance penalty to a recent student checkpoint; optimized with an approximate natural gradient.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Jul 2026]

papers.title: When Top-K Misses the Decision: Tool-Call Drift in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This study audits truncated teacher-logit support in routed tool-use distillation. High retained teacher mass can omit a tool-entry token important to student updates. Restoring student-relevant support improves agreement with full-vocabulary descent, but reduced over-calling is accompanied by lower call recall.
papers.objective: Audit decision-critical coordinates lost under truncated teacher-logit support and test support restoration, loss shaping, and inference entry bias. The current abstract does not specify the revised distillation divergence.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 5 Sep 2026 (this version, v6)]

papers.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Thinking Collapse in On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: AD-OPSD blends a frozen base-model prior into privileged teacher targets at high-entropy positions where sampled tokens face suppression. This selective gate addresses declining epistemic-token density while retaining other teacher corrections; the diagnosis and evaluations focus on mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: Forward KL from a stop-gradient target to the student on student rollouts: the target blends the ground-truth-conditioned teacher with a frozen base-model prior at gated, high-entropy positions and otherwise uses the teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Jul 2026]

papers.title: ShortOPD: Recovering Pruned LLMs with Short-to-Long On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: ShortOPD recovers a structurally pruned student by distilling its pre-pruning self on student-generated rollouts. A controller shortens future rollout horizons when terminal repetition is high and grows them when clean rollouts hit the limit; detected suffixes do not mask the current batch’s loss.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence between frozen teacher and student distributions on student-generated rollouts, with clipped importance weights; apply the loss to all generated tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 14 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Roles, Pathologies, and Regulations
papers.description: This study tests whether OPD improves access to already reachable solutions and diagnoses misleading teacher signals and incentives to pad or truncate responses. It examines clipping and log compression of token advantages, but its coverage and regulation findings come chiefly from mathematical reasoning experiments.
papers.objective: Clipped-ratio policy-gradient updates use sampled-token teacher-minus-student log-probability differences as advantages, either unregulated, bounded by advantage clipping, or signed-log compressed.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Better Starts, Better Ends: Bootstrapped Iterative Self-Reasoning Distillation for Compressed Reasoning
papers.description: BIRD first fine-tunes on answer-correct concise traces generated under a brevity instruction but learned under the original prompt. It then matches a periodically refreshed concise self-teacher on warm-started student prefixes using reverse KL; its reported evaluations concern mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: First maximize the likelihood of correctness-filtered self-generated traces under the original prompt; then minimize token-level student-to-concise-self-teacher KL on student-sampled prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 17 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Trace-Based On-Policy Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.description: TOPD samples a masked diffusion student’s denoising trajectories and retains token decisions that survive into the final response. A frozen teacher supervises matching partially denoised states through reverse KL, implemented with sampled-token updates; the transfer experiments focus on mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: Match student to frozen-teacher token distributions with reverse KL at retained denoising state-position pairs, implemented with a sampled-token score-function estimator using stopped teacher–student log-probability gaps.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 Jul 2026]

papers.title: CriPO: Enhancing Rubric-based RL via Self-Distillation
papers.description: CriPO retains rubric-reward policy optimization on policy-generated responses. A criterion-conditioned self-teacher supplies filtered forward-KL supervision for unmet criteria, while a counterfactual self-teacher locates useful tokens in negative-advantage responses for local advantage flipping. It is a hybrid update, not standalone distillation.
papers.objective: Rubric-reward GRPO with locally corrected token advantages, plus filtered forward KL from the student to a criterion-conditioned self-teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 27 Sep 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
papers.description: For open-ended tasks, a coach turns rubric assessments of policy-generated responses into reusable textual advice that conditions a teacher for token-level reverse-KL distillation along student rollouts. The coach supplies context rather than token probabilities, and the teacher may be frozen or iteratively updated.
papers.objective: Token-level reverse KL from the student distribution to an experiential-advice-conditioned teacher distribution on student-generated responses.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation via Byte-Prefix Marginalization
papers.description: BPM maps teacher next-token probabilities to student tokens through shared byte prefixes, collecting unmatched mass in a residual category before distillation on student rollouts. Exact byte-prefix targets require non-spanning positions; spanning cases use a lower bound, and some positions are masked or excluded.
papers.objective: Generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence between projected student probabilities and byte-prefix teacher targets at included content positions, with forward-KL stop-token bridge supervision.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 24 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Masked Self-Distillation: Internalizing the Chain-of-Thought in Language Models
papers.description: Masked distillation trains on student-sampled continuations using reverse KL toward a teacher conditioned on a collected reasoning trace. A suffix scaffold controls how much reasoning remains explicit; complete trace removal can fail in the evaluated puzzle setting.
papers.objective: Reverse KL from student next-token probabilities to a trace-conditioned teacher on student-sampled continuations; the supervised output includes the answer and, when selected, a trace suffix.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 Jun 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 30 Sep 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Self-Boosting Vision-Language Models with Noisy Student On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: On corrupted-image student rollouts, a vision-language model matches its own stopped-gradient clean-image token distribution using reverse KL. The teacher view shares the student’s parameters rather than supplying external answers; the method depends on visual input corruption.
papers.objective: Reverse KL from the corrupted-image student distribution to the stopped-gradient clean-image self-teacher distribution at student-generated prefixes; sampling is not backpropagated through.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 31 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Outcome-Confounded Local Supervision in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This diagnostic crosses pointwise teacher–student divergence on student-generated math responses with final-answer correctness, showing that local agreement can occur on failed trajectories. Whole-trajectory imitation, masking, and contrast probes do not localize the error; the paper proposes no new training method.
